findings.location: The section, second bullet; Completion criterion 2
findings.problem: The planned text says not to name a relaxed command in any other command and forbids pipes, but the command-permissions spec expressly permits a closed data-position form, including pipelines of read-only tools and single-quoted search terms. This misstates accepted forms, contradicting the plan goal, and can prevent the intended safe search/read workflow.
findings.suggestion: Revise the section and criterion to describe the permitted data-position form precisely (including its limited pipeline syntax), while retaining prohibitions for all other forms.

findings.location: The section, fourth bullet; Completion criterion 2
findings.problem: It says every refusal ends with an alternative form and names only names, gap, and size-limit. The spec says only names and gap refusals provide an alternative; dollar-quote-limit is also a possible named rule, and size-limit has no prescribed replacement form.
findings.suggestion: Distinguish names/gap refusals, which provide a retry form, from size-limit and dollar-quote-limit refusals, which require reporting or shortening/simplifying rather than retrying an asserted hint.

summary: The planned guidance materially drifts from the command-gate specification on allowed data-position commands and refusal handling.
